title: INDIAN CULTURE PORTAL VERSION 2.0
body_text:
Significant measures have been undertaken to strengthen digital access to India's cultural heritage through the upgraded Indian Culture Portal (ICP) Version 2.0, which was launched in March 2026. The upgraded portal has been developed with a modern, scalable, and secure architecture to provide seamless access to India's cultural resources. Key improvements include enhanced search capabilities, multilingual support, improved user interface and user experience, Progressive Web Application (PWA) functionality, AI-enabled chat bot, and integration with cultural institutions of Ministry of Culture.
The initiatives undertaken to improve accessibility, multilingual availability, user interface, public engagement and digital content on the Portal include:
Introduction of a modern and responsive user interface with improved navigation and accessibility. Availability of content in 22 Indian languages through integration with the BHASHINI platform. Deployment of an AI-powered chat bot, Bharti, enabling intelligent search, content discovery and multilingual interaction. Advanced search and filtering features for efficient retrieval of cultural resources. Development of the Portal as a Progressive Web Application (PWA) to enable access across desktops, tablets and mobile devices. Adoption of a decoupled architecture using React and Drupal 10 for improved performance, scalability and security. Addition of new thematic sections and curated cultural collections to enhance public engagement.
The Indian Culture Portal has established mechanisms for integration of cultural institutions through standard metadata exchange, APIs, and institutional onboarding. The Portal serves as a unified discovery platform by aggregating digital resources from museums, libraries, archives, monuments and other cultural institutions under the Ministry of Culture and partner organizations.
The upgraded Portal aims to promote wider public access and preservation of India's cultural heritage by:
Providing a single digital platform for access to cultural resources from multiple institutions. Facilitating research through advanced search, metadata-based discovery and access to digitised collections. Supporting students, researchers, educators and the general public through authenticated cultural information. Enabling virtual exploration of museums, monuments, manuscripts, artworks and heritage collections. Promoting awareness of India's tangible and intangible cultural heritage through curated thematic content. Strengthening long-term digital preservation and accessibility of cultural resources. Encouraging wider public participation through multilingual access and improved digital engagement. Website accessible throughout the globe and responsive in all screen sizes (Desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile phone)
A State/UT-wise list of Institutions integrated with Indian Culture Portal is at Annexure-A .
This information was given by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply in Lok Sabha today

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Culture informed the Lok Sabha that the upgraded Indian Culture Portal (ICP) Version 2.0, launched in March 2026, offers enhanced digital access to India's cultural heritage through features like multilingual support in 22 languages via BHASHINI, an AI chatbot named Bharti, Progressive Web Application functionality, and a modern React-Drupal 10 architecture. The portal aggregates digitised resources from museums, libraries, archives and monuments across multiple states/UTs through institutional integration. This was disclosed by Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a written reply.
enrichment.context:
The Indian Culture Portal is a Ministry of Culture initiative aimed at digitising and democratizing access to India's vast tangible and intangible cultural heritage, aligning with the broader Digital India vision. Its integration with BHASHINI, the National Language Translation Mission under MeitY, reflects a government-wide push to make digital services linguistically inclusive and reduce the English-language barrier to accessing public resources. Such portals also support the government's soft power and cultural diplomacy goals by making India's heritage globally accessible.

This upgrade is part of a continuum of digital cultural heritage projects, including the National Digital Library, National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities, and museum digitisation drives. The involvement of autonomous bodies like Sahitya Akademi, Sangeet Natak Akademi, Lalit Kala Akademi, National Archives of India, and various Zonal Cultural Centres shows an attempt at institutional convergence—bringing together disparate cultural repositories under one discoverable platform. Such convergence is significant for researchers, students and policymakers, as fragmented physical archives across states have historically been a barrier to systematic study of Indian art, history and anthropology. It also ties into UNESCO-linked global efforts on digital preservation of cultural heritage, and India's larger ambitions of heritage tourism and cultural education promotion.

prelims_questions.question: The 'BHASHINI' platform, mentioned in the context of the Indian Culture Portal's multilingual support, is associated with which of the following?
options: National Language Translation Mission under MeitY
Ministry of Culture's heritage digitisation scheme
Ministry of Education's National Digital Library
prelims_questions.explanation: BHASHINI is India's National Language Translation Mission, spearheaded by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), aimed at enabling multilingual digital content and services.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following institutions is NOT mentioned as integrated with the Indian Culture Portal under Delhi (NCT) in the given list?
options: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts
prelims_questions.explanation: Salar Jung Museum is listed under Telangana, not Delhi (NCT), in the Annexure-A list of institutions integrated with the Indian Culture Portal.
